findings.text: Mount namespace ownership can be recovered from the embedded generic namespace member, so the generic member is contained within the larger mount namespace record and serves as the link for container based lookup.
A mount tree is acceptable for relocation only when traversal over its members finds no root that participates in a namespace filesystem loop, with any such loop causing denial.

Loopback duplication permits only suitable sources, denying unbindable mounts, mounts lacking copy permission, dentries carrying DCACHE_NORCU, recursive duplication without an owning namespace, and single duplication shadowed by locked descendants, while recursive requests duplicate a whole tree and nonrecursive requests duplicate one mount.

Tree copy permission is granted for mounts already attached in the caller namespace and for operation vectors ns_dentry_operations and pidfs_dentry_operations, otherwise it requires a visibly mounted mount that also satisfies anonymous mount validation.
An anonymous mount is usable only when its namespace has anonymous character and its origin sequence is either empty or equal to the identifier of the current mount namespace.

Mount reconfiguration holds superblock read protection together with mount hash protection while changing read only state and attributes, releasing both before issuing timestamp expiry warning outside the guarded region.

Locked attributes forbid relaxation of the corresponding mount property, covering read only, device handling, set identifier handling, execution handling, and atime mode, where any mismatch against the locked value denies the change.

Read only transitions are stable when requested and current states agree, entry into read only holds writers before installing the mark and always releases the hold, exit from read only clears the mark directly, and release orders mark visibility before hold removal.
Attribute installation preserves all existing bits outside mask MNT_USER_SETTABLE_MASK, installs caller supplied user bits, and records a touch on the owning mount namespace.

Timestamp expiry warning fires at most once per superblock, only for writable mounts whose time limit approaches within the uptime horizon, and reports filesystem kind, mount versus remount posture, resolved path with unknown fallback, and limit value.

Remount validates namespace membership, mounted path posture, and locked flag compatibility, builds a legacy reconfiguration context constrained to the remount mask, parses monolithic options, then under superblock write protection requires administrative capability before reconfiguring the superblock and updating attributes under hash protection.
Legacy move lookup rejects empty source names, resolves the source with following semantics, and delegates to the general move routine with default flags.

Move relocation requires a mounted source with matching directory character at source and target plus successful target pinning, then applies separate acceptance rules for in namespace sources covering detachability and sharing and for anonymous roots covering namespace distinctness and target usability, and finally denies beneath violations, unbindable trees aimed at shared targets, namespace filesystem loops, and ancestor relations before attach.
Target pinning for move establishes a scoped pinned mountpoint record with automatic release on scope exit and invokes the underlying mount lock helper with the target path and beneath mode.
A tree is deemed to contain an unbindable element when traversal from its root encounters any member marked unbindable.
Ancestor testing walks parent links upward from the possible descendant until either reaching the possible ancestor or exhausting parenthood, reporting kinship only on reaching the ancestor.

Beneath relocation denies sources carrying an overmount, denies placements where the destination is an ancestor of the source, and denies two propagation hazards where parent sharing would place a copy over the destination or over the source itself.
Propagation overmount risk exists only for shared sources whose destination root aligns with the mountpoint dentry and where some master in the destination chain peers with the source.
A move target is immediately usable when resident in the caller namespace, otherwise it must remain visibly mounted and satisfy anonymous mount validation.

New mount creation requires a filesystem type name, resolves the type, validates optional subtype syntax, builds a legacy mount context, parses subtype plus source plus monolithic options in sequence, checks mount capability, and delegates to the context mount helper.

Context based mount instantiates the filesystem mount, applies a security mount check, rejects overly revealing superblocks for restricted types, issues timestamp warning, then pins the mountpoint and adds the mount while consuming the transient reference only on success.

Overly revealing assessment is bypassed in the initial user namespace and for unrestricted filesystem kinds, requires restricted superblocks to carry no execution and no device marks, bypasses restricted variants, and otherwise demands a preexisting visible mount.

Visibility reuse scans the namespace visible list for same type nonrestricted candidates with compatible read only and atime posture and without locked coverings over nonempty directories, and on success carries locked read only and atime posture into the proposed flags.
Permanent directory emptiness holds only when both the file operation vector and the inode operation vector equal their dedicated empty directory values.
Filesystem context logging helper records an error entry with a caller supplied prefix and formatted detail into the context log.
Early unmount resolves a mountpoint path with following behavior controlled by a nofollow flag and delegates to path based unmount.
Path based unmount checks unmount permission before attempting removal and releases references with expiry mark preserving semantics.

Unmount distinguishes expiry, force, root, and detach postures, with expiry enforcing nonroot status and flag exclusivity plus busy and retry handling, force invoking an optional abort hook, root without detach attempting a read only transition under capability check, and general removal under namespace and hash protection either detaching or shrinking before conditional synchronous removal when idle.

Namespace release drains pending unmounted and mountpoint lists, downgrades to shared protection while delivering notifications to permit concurrent readers, frees any emptied namespace after leak warning, shrinks dentries, and after an expedited grace period drops references for unmounted members.
Mount namespace emptiness is determined solely by whether its mount tree root holds no entries.

Mount notification delivery is configuration dependent, with enabled builds draining a pending list through per mount notification and list reinitialization plus nonempty pending detection, while disabled builds provide inert delivery and constant negative pending detection.

Per mount notification classifies transitions by comparing previous and current namespace links into attach, detach, move within one namespace, and cross namespace transfer combining detach plus attach, then synchronizes the stored previous link, with thin wrappers forwarding distinct event kinds to a common backend that may be inert.
Mount namespace destruction bypasses generic release for anonymous namespaces, decrements usage accounting, emits deletion notification, and detaches from the global tree with deferred reclamation.
Mount namespace state includes an owning user namespace, an origin sequence for anonymous validation, a visible mount list for reuse checks, and a mount tree root for emptiness testing.

Mount linkage combines an embedded virtual mount record with parent and master links, child and sibling membership, mountpoint and overmount pointers, owning namespace and previous namespace links, plus expiry, notification, and unmount queue state.
Propagation overmount test is usable across compilation units for validating beneath placements.
Empty directory inode test is usable across compilation units for visibility and covering checks.
Early unmount helper is available during initialization for removing mounts by path name.
Path based unmount helper is available to callers holding a resolved path and flag set.

Invalid request status EINVAL signals unsuitable loopback sources, nonmember reconfigure targets, nonmember remount targets, empty move names, mismatched directory character, detachability violations, sharing violations, beneath violations, unbindable into shared placements, and related malformed mount requests.
Permission status EPERM signals locked flag relaxation attempts, capability failures during remount and root handling, mount capability failures, and overly revealing mounts.

Distinct statuses signal contended unmount with EBUSY, namespace loop or ancestor move with ELOOP, first expiry marking with EAGAIN, unknown filesystem type with ENODEV, and name buffer shortage with ENOMEM.

Mount flag family MNT_READONLY plus MNT_NODEV plus MNT_NOSUID plus MNT_NOEXEC plus atime mask plus user settable mask plus locked counterparts governs attribute preservation, relaxation denial, and visibility compatibility.

Visibility scanning acquires shared namespace protection, remount reconfiguration acquires exclusive superblock protection, and context mount addition acquires mountpoint protection during tree insertion.

Unmount notification and reclamation ordering requires event sequencing under locks, shared protection during delivery, and deferred reference drops only after a grace period, preventing use after free for concurrent readers.
